message: Imported canonical English Task 2 fixture Context 'advisor2/style' into profile 'task-2-proposal-authority'.

9bd2a9da-9720-5001-b958-f7a2a2658f87.content: Use an em dash only for a deliberate interruption or sharp contrast; otherwise split the sentence or choose ordinary punctuation.

e3e20261-e03c-52fb-be9e-04f5f9b1294d.content: Write repeatable user study procedures so that tasks and steps precede people.

8d8d0e8d-dad1-50b5-9438-049052748a6a.content: Write system behaviors confirmed in the actual usage environment as observed states.

8c74ba87-822b-5ce2-9a3a-3adc02ab9744.content: Write system behaviors not yet confirmed in the field as conditional plans.

1f29de31-5429-5dfc-ab27-01779fa16704.content: HCI reviewers easily identify repeatable user study procedures in sentences where tasks and steps precede people.

1d181223-f750-57d2-97a5-b79f276a589f.content: Do not mechanically split connected thoughts into separate short sentences when doing so destroys the intended reading rhythm.

a5ce5f9f-8852-5080-ae35-21abcf4a0973.content: Preserve a longer sentence when its clauses form one continuous movement that is easier to follow together than apart.

888ce8af-a36e-5e74-9a0c-604aac48d3b7.content: The user writing this proposal understands that short sentences are easier to scan but feels that uniformly segmented prose loses its reading rhythm.

ddf40413-3274-5662-ba5e-d6cae2a1e546.content: When describing field interactions, explicitly specify the actor, action, and target system at each step.

6b7aaddf-5bbd-5015-811d-9f4d7a4b4ad1.content: The agent cannot identify who is responsible for error handling in field procedures written exclusively in passive voice.

89c2ce30-d6aa-5762-bf17-c697caac68e4.content: Because operational procedures and user roles remain undefined, the mechanisms behind expected behavioral changes are provisional when conditional features have not yet been approved by field partners.

9f1b647a-bd2b-50df-8141-5b8c142c0fa5.content: The user writing this proposal can explain whether an em dash marks an intentional interruption or contrast rather than using it decoratively.

49a42872-adcc-5bf8-9029-1d134cac6267.content: An em dash creates a stronger interruption than a comma and can make a deliberate contrast easier to hear in the sentence.
